profile.campus: EdgeCore Mesa/Phoenix campus, AZ (84 acres, 5 buildings)
profile.reading: EdgeCore's Mesa, Arizona campus sits at 3856 South Everton Terrace, Mesa, Arizona, within the Greater Phoenix market; the operator's own dedicated campus page names the location Phoenix in its marketing but explicitly states the physical location as Mesa, Arizona, resolving an earlier naming ambiguity this registry had flagged. EdgeCore's own site describes an 84 acre campus totaling 2.7 million square feet across 5 data center buildings, with 496 megawatts of critical IT load, among the larger hyperscale campuses in the Phoenix metro data center market alongside other operators tracked elsewhere in this registry. The operator's own page does not publish a street address; the address applied here comes from a dedicated aggregator listing for this exact EdgeCore Mesa facility, applied given the operator's own confirmation that Mesa is this campus's true municipal location. EdgeCore is a hyperscale data center developer and operator building large scale campuses for cloud and enterprise tenants requiring substantial critical IT load, with additional campuses including a Silicon Valley, California site already on file elsewhere in this registry. Phoenix and its surrounding suburbs, including Mesa and Chandler, have become one of the fastest growing US hyperscale data center markets over the past decade, drawing developers with relatively low land and power costs, low natural disaster risk, and a state sales and use tax exemption program for qualifying data center equipment purchases. EdgeCore's Arizona campus draws power in part from Salt River Project and Arizona Public Service, the two major regional utilities that have expanded transmission capacity in recent years specifically to serve the growing cluster of hyperscale campuses across Mesa, Chandler, and Goodyear, positioning the region as one of the largest concentrations of hyperscale critical IT load in the western United States alongside Northern Virginia and Texas.

reading.body:
The EdgeCore Mesa campus in Arizona publishes 496 megawatts of IT load across 2.7 million square feet in five buildings on 84 acres. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack as a common AI training density, 496 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 12,400 racks, a scale sufficient to host large-scale AI model training and inference workloads. The campus certifications and specific tenant deployments are not published.

Arizona has published capacity of 512 megawatts across four facilities with disclosed figures. EdgeCore Mesa represents 97 percent of the state's published data center IT capacity and ranks fifth among all 56 mapped facilities in Arizona, though most mapped facilities disclose no power specifications. This concentration reflects the state's limited disclosure of operating capacity rather than an exhaustive count of deployments.

The state context provided does not include information about Arizona's grid constraints, power procurement, or available interconnection capacity. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on factors not in the published specifications: the campus's actual utilization, the availability of incremental power and cooling at this site, and Arizona's ability to supply reliable electricity to additional AI infrastructure. The operator's own pages do not publish these details.
